explanation: The statement is a very specific half-pairing identity: the sum over j in [1,p) of f(ζ^j) equals twice the sum over k in [1,p/2] when f is inversion-invariant and ζ is a primitive p-th root of unity with p odd. I searched Mathlib for sums over `Icc 1 (p/2)` and `Ico 1 p`, and for the helper names used in the proof. The only hits were in NumberTheory (Wilson, Bernoulli, Gauss-Eisenstein lemmas). None of them states this identity or a general form of it. The proof relies on library-local helpers (`sum_Ico_eq_sum_half_pair`, `inv_zetaPow`).
